anatomy.intro: A low rosette combines fleshy leaves, a growing center and smaller offsets.

parts.function: The thick blade stores water and carries out photosynthesis.
parts.label: Fleshy leaf

parts.function: The narrow colored edge outlines each leaf and may intensify with stronger light.
parts.label: Red margin

parts.function: Successive young leaves expand from the center.
parts.label: Rosette center

parts.function: A daughter rosette can develop beside the original plant.
parts.label: Basal offset

flowers.text: The species has small yellow, urn-shaped flowers that hang from long curved stalks. Flower shape and color would be useful additional identification evidence for this probable plant; foliage alone leaves room for similar hybrids.

growth.note: These are possible stages, not a timetable; a close hybrid may differ in flower details.

stages.text: New central leaves enlarge while older leaves form the outer tiers.
stages.title: Build a rosette

stages.text: Side rosettes can gradually turn one crown into a small group.
stages.title: Add offsets

stages.text: An established rosette may send an arching stalk above its leaves.
stages.title: Raise a flower stalk

habitat.text: The species comes from Hidalgo, Puebla and Veracruz in Mexico, where Kew places it in desert or dry shrubland. Its compact succulent rosette belongs to that setting; it is not a tropical foliage plant. This collection plant remains probable E. pulidonis or a close hybrid, so the species story provides context rather than proof of its identity.

lookalikes.name: Echeveria 'Raindrops'
lookalikes.text: Both form blue-green rosettes, but mature 'Raindrops' develops rounded raised bumps; probable pulidonis has smooth blades with a narrow red outline.

mature.text: RHS describes individual rosettes reaching about 12 cm across. Offsets can broaden the group, while flowering stalks rise above the low leaf crown. That species scale is a reference, not a prediction for a shaded corner of the shared planter.

milestones.text: Acquired at Gerych's Greenhouse in the shared square succulent planter, now tracked as P20 / #2.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

nameStory.text: Kew records the name Echeveria pulidonis as published by E. Walther in 1972. The botanical name and the collection's probable identification are separate facts.
